messages:
Samir Khan: Quick follow-up from the post-RFC sync: I'm proposing a "staged-pin" primitive instead of full token handoffs. API sketch: `staged_pin(id, ttl_ms=?, priority=0)` + `unpin(id)`. Staged pins are soft: they bias the evictor but still allow preemption under global pressure. Thoughts?

Priya Iyer: Staged-pin sounds much simpler for SDKs. Two immediate concerns: 1) how do we surface preemption to callers (so they can retry or re-warm), and 2) what prevents a tenant from flooding with low-ttl pins and hurting eviction fairness?

Ben Thompson: For (1) we can emit a preempt event via the existing eviction-notify webhook with an extra field `preempted_by_pressure:true` and include a suggested retry-backoff_ms. For (2) global admission + per-tenant token-bucket should work; treat staged-pins as a soft-allocated quota that counts against a tenant's frag budget.

Zoe Li: Microbench results from my branch where staged-pin replaces LeaseToken:
```
workload: mixed-chat (rps 1200)
median p99 p95
baseline: 15ms 120ms 45ms
staged-pin: 16ms 145ms 55ms
rewarm cost: +18% token ops reduced
```
We see slight tail impact but ops cost down ~20%. Also fragmentation index (measured as free-run variance) reduced when we add a periodic coalesce pass.

Samir Khan: Good data. Coalesce pass = expensive? We should avoid long stop-the-world operations. Zoe, what's the coalesce runtime at host scale?

Zoe Li: On our canary host (A100, 512GB), incremental coalesce that merges small adjacent free buckets takes ~120ms per pass and can be rate-limited. Full compaction is expensive (seconds), but we only need incremental coalesce to keep fragmentation from spiraling.

Priya Iyer: I'm worried about observability: operators need a clear metric to know when staged-pins are causing frag pressure. Suggest `tenant_frag_score` + `staged_pin_active_count` + `preemptions/sec`. Add alert if frag_score > 0.7 and preemptions/sec > 5.

Ben Thompson: Good alerts. Also propose a demotion policy for pinned entries: demote if not touched for demote_after_ms and if tenant_frag_score > tenant_frag_budget. Keeps default UX friendly but controlled.

Samir Khan: How about default demote_after_ms=120000 and a per-tenant frag_budget that scales with committed capacity? Low-risk rollout: staged-pin FF disabled, coalesce experimental on a small fleet, preempt webhook enabled for canary only.

infra-bot: feature-flag memory.staged_pin created. Canary rollout scheduled: group=canary-a, start=Tue 03:00 UTC. Dashboards: /d/memory/staged-pin (owner: @Samir).

Zoe Li: I'll land the coalesce rate-limiter and add a non-blocking async compaction worker. Also will add timestamps to eviction-notify so clients can correlate.

Priya Iyer: I'll draft the SDK guidance: use staged_pin for hot KV (e.g., model prompt caches), avoid making every request pinned, subscribe to eviction webhook, implement jittered retry. Include sample code.

Ben Thompson: I'll add the per-tenant quota enforcement and simulate mixed workloads with tenant traces (Q4_replay + synthetic_longtail). Want to test failure modes: all tenants pin -> ensure graceful degradation.

Samir Khan: Action items: Zoe coalesce + eviction timestamps, Ben quota + sim, Priya SDK docs + webhook schema, Samir coordinate rollout gates (p95, frag_score, preemptions). Keep sticky-like permanent pins off for now. We'll reconvene after sims.

Priya Iyer: One more UX idea: add `pin_hint("hot_prefix")` so customers can indicate semantic importance; we treat hints as lower priority than explicit staged_pin but higher than ephemeral. Might help clients that can't track TTLs.

Zoe Li: Interesting, but hints complicate quota. Could be an opt-in knob. Add to RFC draft.

Samir Khan: OK. Please drop RFC link here when ready. Also prefer initial canary to limit staged_pin rate to 1% of requests so we can measure marginal impact.

Ben Thompson: Will do, starting sims tomorrow.

infra-bot: canary created (id: canary-2026-06-01-07).
